PullRequest.Title: sessions: Fix empty cloud sandbox resume views
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fix two client paths that can leave a resumed Copilot Cloud sandbox showing an empty conversation even after its live connection succeeds:

- Session activation now joins an explicit wake already in progress, including one that starts during the environment lookup, rather than opening an offline-history stand-in while the sandbox is waking. Failed wakes still fall back to persisted history, and merely opening a dormant environment still does not wake it.
- Mission Control history replay honors the host-announced default chat and, when none was announced, uses an unambiguous sole recorded chat instead of seeding an empty `<session>/chat`. Recorded catalogues identifying another chat or a tool, side, or fork origin prevent that inference. Multiple conversations remain separate.

Add regression coverage for successful and failed pending wakes, a wake racing the environment lookup, opaque recorded chat URIs, explicit empty defaults, ambiguous histories, and peer-chat catalogue metadata.

This replay path is used for Mission Control offline cloud history, not ordinary live VS Code agent-host restoration. Shared protocol reducers and live host session restoration are unchanged.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed. The first run caught missing required display names in two new test connection options; those were fixed and compilation was rerun successfully.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/taskEventReplay.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 158 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/taskEventReplay.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/taskEventReplay.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxSessionContribution.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Commit-time hygiene checks — passed.
- The initial resume/default-chat regression tests failed against the previous implementation; the peer-chat guard tests also failed before the guard was added.

## Manual verification

Not yet verified against a live cloud sandbox. Resume a dormant sandbox and open its conversation while the wake is in progress; once connected, the existing transcript should load rather than remain on an empty offline-history view. Opening a dormant sandbox without explicitly resuming it should still display read-only persisted history without waking it.

When recordings omit both the default pointer and distinguishing catalogue metadata, the sole-chat inference cannot prove that no unrecorded peer exists. Explicit defaults and available catalogue evidence remain authoritative.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a dormant cloud sandbox session from Mission Control persisted history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat-session resolution calls _waitForActivation, waits for one Mission Control environment-status request, registers the read-only provider when offline, and then the first content resolution waits for the prefetched task-events request and synchronous decode/fold before the transcript can render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the sandbox environment record to determine whether it is online
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for a normal activation; independent of event or chat count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same status request occurred before the diff for a dormant environment without an already-pending connect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before choosing live connection versus history.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET /tasks/<taskId>/events, parse the complete JSON response, and replay its AHP frames
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One prefetched request for the first history-backed open; later opens issue one fresh request each, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same prefetched history request and replay occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The transcript cannot render until the response and O(E) replay complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The HTTP response contains E persisted transport events across S sessions and C chat catalogue entries. Replay already decodes and folds E events; the diff adds four constant action-type comparisons per session action and one O(C) catalogue scan per folded session, with C normally much smaller than E and dominated by existing reducer/replay work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A normal open performs one status request and one prefetched history request. The read-only handler consumes that promise once; later opens intentionally fetch fresh history. Concurrent activation coalescing is unchanged by the diff, and no loop fans out boundary calls by event or chat.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no environment-status cache on this path. The first history read uses the activation's one-shot prefetched promise, while subsequent content resolutions read fresh history so stale transcripts are not pinned. The changed default-chat inference does not add retained cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the traced activation, API, replay, and read-only-provider call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Mission Control history sizes and catalogue cardinalities are not measured here, but the added O(C) terminal scan is dominated by the existing full event replay and does not change boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds only bounded in-memory checks after the existing full replay and introduces no new request, fan-out, concurrency, or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a sandbox conversation while an explicit wake/connect is already succeeding
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activation now joins the existing per-address pending connect, then waits for the registered relay connection's root state to advertise the requested provider. This intentionally moves the already-running wake and relay handshake onto the open's critical path so a temporary offline-history provider cannot win the session resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Mission Control credential/wake request followed by Web PubSub relay establishment and AHP handshake
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one already-running connect per sandbox address, shared by activation and the explicit wake caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The explicit wake still incurred this boundary, but activation did not join it; activation could instead status-check and resolve against offline history while wake continued.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff makes activation await the existing wake and live host advertisement; it does not create a second wake request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One sandbox address/session open. Cost is governed by wake duration and relay handshake latency, not collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: _pendingConnects coalesces all callers for an address onto one promise; calling connect from activation reuses that promise and does not mint another credential or establish another relay. Different addresses remain independent, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No response cache is used. The pending-connect map is a short-lived positive in-flight entry removed in finally on success or failure; successful connection state is then reused by the agent-host service.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the critical-path join is real and coalesced because both changed pending-map checks lead synchronously to connect, which returns the stored per-address promise.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A cold wake can take minutes according to the connection-path comments, but prevalence and observed timings are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: moving the existing explicit wake onto activation is the required scheduling change, while coalescing prevents added network work and the initial pending case now avoids the separate environment-status request.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a sandbox conversation while an explicit wake is pending and then fails
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activation joins the one existing wake attempt. After that promise rejects, it registers the read-only provider and the first session resolution waits for persisted task history. This delays fallback until failure is known, preserving successful-wake handoff semantics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await the already-running Mission Control wake/credential request and relay connection attempt
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared attempt per address, regardless of concurrent callers reaching connect while its pending entry exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Activation could status-check the environment and serve history while the separate explicit wake was still pending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff places the pending wake before history fallback; a failure must settle before activation can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and replay persisted task events after wake failure
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One prefetched request for the fallback provider's first open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same history request existed, but for an offline status it could begin before the separate wake settled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after the failed wake and must complete before rendering the transcript.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One wake attempt and one history response containing E persisted events; no per-event or per-chat boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The connect remains one shared per-address attempt. On failure, the activation starts one history request for the provider's first open; there is no new burst introduced by the changed lines.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The failed pending entry is removed in connect's finally. The fallback history promise is passed to the handler and consumed once; later opens fetch fresh state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in ordering and boundary count from _waitForActivation, the per-address pending map, and connect's catch/finally lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure frequency and typical time-to-failure are unknown; the connection attempt is bounded by existing timeout/cancellation behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the latency shift is an intentional, bounded correctness tradeoff needed to avoid resolving a stand-in while an explicit wake may succeed; the diff neither duplicates the wake nor increases boundary cardinality, and a failed wake still falls back through the existing history path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files. Traced offline replay, successful concurrent wake, and failed-wake fallback through network boundaries, replay scaling, cache lifetime, and per-address connect coalescing. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying shipped-regression fix was found.
